message:
test(apk): the queue-age metric by the AU's own identity; honest labels; the relay trace counts arrived bytes (keepalive-r2 e, Codex apk-inbox plan src r1)

No policy change; trace builds / the local fixture's relay trace only.
- sink: an AU's enqueue time is kept by its identity (stream generation + seq, a 64-slot ring) and read when THAT
  AU goes into the codec -- r1 read the last-processed frame's time (Codex reproduced a held IDR's ~286 ms as 33 ms).
  Replays are counted apart, an AU the ring lost is `unmatched` (never another's time).
- labels: inboxHw = admitted after the trim, inboxPeakPre = including the frame just added; rxLockScopeMax (an upper
  bound of the hold: the scope's end); createCfgStart (one span, not three calls).
- android_decoder_inbox_test [6] (built with GNLINK_LIVENESS_TRACE): an IDR held ~250 ms for an input buffer, a
  delta after it -> ageQueue max 280 ms (it waited ~283 ms) PASS; the 8868fb5 sink: 31 ms FAIL. [1]-[5] unchanged
  (the baseline: their expected FAILs stay).
- server.js relay trace (REMOTE60_RELAY_TRACE=1 only): the UDP payload bytes that ARRIVED per flow and direction --
  cumulative in each line (rxBytes c2h=B/n h2c=B/n), and per 1 s bucket at the close (`<key>B`); counted at rx only.
  relay_trace_test: exact for the known lengths (49-byte Hello, 1200-byte media) ALL PASS.
Regression: liveness 68, idr_recovery 49 (trace on), session 9, owed 32, binding 17, decode_stats 42, geometry 10;
NDK buildCMakeDebug plain and trace OK.
